subject: POC: Prompt set + eval dataset collection / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: POC: Prompt set + eval dataset collection / next steps

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off the POC smoothly: 

- Scope: Evaluate Redwood inference on Acme Health support ticket summarization and triage prompts (3 workloads: short triage, long-case summarization, priority classification).
- Success criteria (proposal):
  - Accuracy: ≥85% match to your current human labels on priority classification on holdout set
  - Latency: median inference ≤350ms for short triage prompts under POC load (see proposed QPS below)
  - Cost: token/unit cost estimate delivered within first week of runs
- Deliverables from Acme: a) prompt set + example inputs (csv preferred), b) current human labels for evaluation (holdout), c) expected throughput profile (QPS, concurrency), d) any redaction rules.
- Redwood deliverables: POC eval plan, model/config recommendations, initial runs and eval dashboard, and a short results review.
- Timeline (proposed):
  - Tue 2/24: Acme shares prompt set + 3 sample batches (10–50 examples each)
  - Wed 2/25: Redwood shares detailed eval plan and run schedule
  - Mon 3/2: Initial runs complete; share preliminary dashboard
  - Wed 3/4: Sync to review results and next steps

Can you confirm ownership on your side for the dataset and who will share the files? Also attaching a draft eval plan (pdf) and a CSV template for the prompt set to make this easier.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_poc_eval_plan.pdf (PDF stub), acme_prompt_samples_template.csv (CSV stub)

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt set + eval dataset collection / next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. Quick answers:

- I'll own the dataset and share the files. Tom will pull the historical tickets and labels.
- We can provide three buckets as you requested: triage_short.csv, summarization_long.csv, priority_labels.csv. Expect ~2k rows total (mix of anonymized tickets).
- Redaction: PHI already redacted but please confirm if you need further hashing/ID mapping.
- QPS: expect peak of ~5 rps for triage during business hours; average 0.8 rps. Concurrency low (<=3).

I'll upload the initial sample files by 2/24 EOD.

One question from Tom: do you have a recommended format for the human labels file? We currently use a mix of free-text tags and a priority integer (1–5).

—Jane
Product Manager, Acme Health

Attachments: (will upload samples 2/24)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-22T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt set + eval dataset collection / next steps

Hi Jane — thanks for confirming. A couple quick notes on labels/format to make the eval straightforward: 

- For priority classification: a single column named "priority_label" with integer values 1–5 is ideal. If you also have free-text tags, include them in a separate column ("tags") so we can map where necessary.
- For summarization: provide original_text and reference_summary columns. If you have multiple human references, include them as reference_summary_1, _2, etc.
- For triage/short prompts: a single input column (ticket_text) and an expected output/intent column is fine.

We'll convert to Redwood's eval schema on our side but having consistent column names speeds up onboarding. 

Also attaching a quick CSV example (acme_prompt_samples.csv) with the exact headers we prefer. If you prefer, we can accept a JSONL as well.

Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_prompt_samples.csv (CSV stub)

Thanks Jane — got the files and the mapping, this is perfect. Next steps from our side: 

1) We'll load the datasets into a private POC workspace and run a schema check today. If any columns need normalizing we'll ping you with a short list (expected by EOD 2/25).
2) By 2/26 we'll run baseline inference using our suggested family (open LLM vX quantized) and provide an initial eval report.
3) We'll share a short dashboard (link will be posted here) and a summary PDF by 3/2 as Marissa outlined.

Owner for Redwood delivery: Rishi Malhotra (I'll be the primary for runs and liaise with Aditya on label mapping).

If this looks right, Marissa and I will schedule the 3/4 review slot and share a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Rishi
